extracted.intended_audience: prospective depositors of biological material (patent applicants), patent agents, and IDA administrators seeking procedural/technical rules for deposits under the Budapest Treaty
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural, technical and administrative requirements and practices that International Depositary Authorities (IDAs) follow for accepting, storing, testing and furnishing microorganisms and related biological material under the Budapest Treaty (guidance for depositors and patent agents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of Microorganisms that May Be Deposited
rubrics_metrics.description: The different types of biological entities accepted for deposit and any specific exclusions are given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDAs list which kinds they accept and any exclusions and may state maximum hazard rating/containment acceptable. Examples: CBA will accept human and animal cell lines and hybridomas preservable in liquid nitrogen vapour but will not accept genetically modified organisms requiring physical containment level 3 or 4 (PC3 or PC4). NMI accepts bacteria (including actinomycetes), yeasts and fungi other than known human and animal pathogens; nucleic acid preparations and phages may be accepted if depositor certifies no hazard. BCCMTM collections accept samples that can be cultured and preserved under technically feasible conditions and impose limits by hazard/risk group (e.g., exclusion of agents above specified risk groups).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum hazard rating / physical containment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum hazard rating and/or physical containment requirements acceptable to the IDA in respect of microorganisms that may be deposited are stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDAs may explicitly refuse deposits requiring high-level containment or otherwise hazardous handling (e.g., CBA excludes PC3/PC4 GMOs; BCCMTM excludes materials whose manipulation/conservation involves excessive hazards; some IDAs accept only non-pathogenic organisms or up to Risk Group 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and Quantity (state of cultures, minimum replicates and titre)
rubrics_metrics.description: The state in which cultures must be submitted (lyophilized, frozen, liquid suspension, agar slant, etc.), the minimum number of replicates and the minimum titre of each culture (where appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per-IDAs have specific requirements: CBA requires frozen cultures, a minimum of 12 replicates and hybridoma/human/animal cultures must contain at least 4 x 10^6 cells/ampoule. NMI requires bacteria/fungi/yeasts as 6 lyophilized or on culture media; phages/plasmids sufficient quantity and titre for preservation. BCCMTM often requires 23 ampoules freeze-dried for bacteria/filamentous fungi/yeasts/actinomycetes (with minimum fallbacks like 3 ampoules), 3 active/frozen cultures for plasmids-in-host, 2 x 1-2 ml cryotubes x≥12 for human/animal cell cultures (≥4 x 10^6 viable cells/vial), plasmid DNA minimum 2 x 20 μg, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Required for Viability Testing
rubrics_metrics.description: The average and maximum length of time (in days) needed by the IDA to carry out viability tests is given for each kind of microorganism accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDAs publish typical test durations but note times may be longer. Examples: CBA—animal/human/hybridoma cultures 10 days (or up to 15 days); NMI—bacteria 5 days, fungi 10 days, yeasts 10 days; BCCMTM—bacteria 3 days, filamentous fungi 3 days, yeasts 2 days, arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi ~30 days, plasmids ~1 week, human/animal cell cultures ≈3 weeks. Depositors are warned viability tests can take longer in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor Checks and Renewal of Stocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Information whether the IDA subcultures material supplied by the depositor to provide stocks; whether it stores samples originally supplied by the depositor; how it replenishes diminishing stocks; and whether it requires the depositor to test for authenticity samples of its own preparations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practices vary: CBA generally does not prepare its own batches and will ask the depositor to make a new deposit when stocks are depleted; CBA asks the depositor to check authenticity of samples prepared by CBA. NMI prepares its own batches by subculturing, stores original material, may prepare new batches with depositor approval, and asks the depositor to check authenticity at deposit and thereafter. BCCMTM will prepare stocks (e.g., 20 cryopreserved samples) and specifies procedures for replenishment and depositor authenticity checks; exceptions and case-by-case arrangements exist for material that cannot be conserved except by active culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: The official language(s) and any other language(s) in which the IDA accepts communications are given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: CBA official language is English and communications in any other language are not accepted; NMI official language is English. Other IDAs list their official/accepted languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract / Terms and Conditions of Deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about the kind of contract (if any) that the IDA enters into with the depositor and the terms and conditions binding the depositor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some IDAs require completion of application forms that bind the depositor to specific obligations (e.g., CBA application form binds depositor to provide material only in required form/quantity, provide biohazard statement, pay fees, observe Treaty terms, accept deposit terms). NMI currently does not enter into a written contract defining liabilities. IDA-specific terms are described in each IDA's section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Import and/or Quarantine Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether any of the microorganisms accepted by the IDA are subject to import and/or quarantine regulations; requirements for compliance; and government departments for advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDAs state their expectations and may assist: CBA requires appropriate regulatory documentation before acceptance and advises depositors to obtain documentation once a biohazard statement is received. NMI will arrange necessary permits for importation and clearance of quarantine requirements but asks the depositor to contact NMI before deposit. IDAs give specifics about documents and contacts (e.g., Australian Quarantine Inspection Service).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements to Be Met by the Depositor When Making the Original Deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to any forms that must be completed; any information that must be given to the IDA in advance of deposit; and any special transport and/or delivery arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model/international forms (BP/1, BP/4, BP/9, BP/7 etc.) are often required. Examples: CBA requires a deposit form and biohazard statement; at least 48 hours before dispatch CBA must be informed of number of ampoules, method of transportation and ETA; if by air, flight, waybill and handling agent details. NMI requests model form BP/1 and BP/7 for later amendments. Specific shipping/packing requirements (e.g., sufficient dry ice) are listed and IDAs may refuse deposits not properly packed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official and Unofficial Notifications to the Depositor
rubrics_metrics.description: What official forms are used for receipts and viability statements, and whether the IDA will issue unofficial advance communications (telephone, fax, email) about deposit status or viability results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory international forms BP/4 (receipt) and BP/9 (viability statement) are commonly used. IDAs may also provide unofficial notifications: CBA can telephone/fax/email date of deposit and accession number on request and may inform depositors of viability only where viability is unacceptably low; NMI will telephone/telex date and accession number and communicate viability test results before formal issuance if requested. Attestation of receipt of later indications uses form BP/8, notification of furnished sample uses BP/14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply of Information to a Patent Agent
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the IDA will supply copies of documents (receipts, viability statements) to the depositor's patent agent and whether the IDA requests patent agent contact details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practices vary: CBA does not routinely ask for patent attorney information but will send copies of receipt and viability statement to the depositor's patent attorney if requested. NMI asks the depositor at time of deposit for name/address of patent agent and will send copies to both depositor and patent agent if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converting a Previous Deposit to a Budapest Treaty Deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about the requirements to convert a deposit previously made outside the Treaty to one made under the Budapest Treaty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion by the original depositor is generally permitted whether or not originally deposited for patent purposes, but converted deposits are subject to standard Budapest Treaty storage fees. Administrative requirements for conversion are the same as for an original deposit except shipping procedures may not apply; some IDAs also request depositor verification of authenticity at conversion (e.g., NMI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Making a New Deposit (after an original deposit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any requirements of the IDA additional to those that must be met when making an original deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDAs require completion of specific forms for new deposits (e.g., BP/2 for NMI) and submission of copies of documents specified under Rule 6.2; otherwise procedures mirror original deposit requirements. Some IDAs require the depositor to submit declaration copies and adhere to shipping requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for Samples and Furnishing of Samples (procedures and requester obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the IDA advises third parties of correct procedures to make a valid request; whether it supplies appropriate forms; whether requesting party must meet health and safety requirements; and whether samples furnished are from IDA preparations or depositor-supplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDAs differ: CBA does not advise requesting parties or supply request forms for proof-of-entitlement requests (these come from the relevant office) and usually furnishes samples from preparations supplied by the depositor; CBA withholds potentially hazardous microorganisms until requester confirms appropriate containment and assumes overseas requesters have met their import requirements. NMI advises requesting parties, supplies model request form BP/12 and/or industrial property office forms, and furnishes dangerous microorganisms only after confirmation the requester can handle them safely. IDAs indicate whether they supply the appropriate request forms and safety guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of the Depositor upon Furnishing Samples
rubrics_metrics.description: The means whereby the IDA notifies the depositor of the furnishing of samples to third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many IDAs notify depositors by letter when samples are furnished (e.g., CBA, NMI). IDAs specify which form is used for notification (e.g., BP/14) and procedures for informing depositors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cataloguing of Budapest Treaty Deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether, and under what conditions, the IDA lists deposits under the Budapest Treaty in its published catalogs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some IDAs publish deposits in their catalogues subject to conditions; others do not. Examples: CBA does not list Budapest Treaty deposits in its published catalogue; NMI does not publish a catalog at present. IDAs state their cataloguing policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The fees payable to the IDA for procedures carried out under the Budapest Treaty (storage, issuance of viability statements, furnishing samples, certifications, administration fees, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each IDA lists its fee schedule. Examples: CBA (AUD) — storage including certification and viability statement 2,600; issuance of new/updated viability statement 170; furnishing of a sample 210; issuance of (new/amended) certification 110; administration fee for amendments 110. NMI (AUD) — storage 1,000; issuance of viability statement on existing deposit 270; furnishing of a sample 270. BCCMTM and others list fees and may add GST/VAT where applicable. Fees and billing policies vary by IDA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for Depositors (publications and help)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to any publications or guidance that the IDA makes available for prospective depositors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDAs provide guidance notes, application forms and website information for depositors. Examples: CBA guidance is provided on the CBA application form and website; NMI indicates guidance notes for prospective depositors are in preparation; IDAs often reference WIPO/Budapest model/international forms and WIPO website for up-to-date lists of accepted kinds and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Requirements for Specific Types of Material (plasmids, arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi, human/animal cell lines, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific technical criteria and preparation requirements for particular classes of biological material (e.g., plasmids in hosts, plasmid DNA isolated, arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi, human/animal cell cultures, phages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed per-type rules are provided. Examples from BCCMTM: plasmids as isolated material must be supplied freeze-dried/frozen or precipitated in alcohol with minimum 2 x 20 μg and sufficient purity for transformation; recommended bacterial host strain must be stated and provided if not available; plasmids in a bacterial host: three active/freeze-dried/frozen cultures required. Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi: optimally supply 2 monoxenic in vitro cultures or an inoculum with propagules derived from a single monosporal culture; BCCMTM may attempt in vitro culture for a fee. Human/animal cell cultures and hybridomas must be checked for contaminants, supplied as mass frozen cultures containing at least 4 x 10^6 viable cells/vial and at least 12 samples in well-sealed 1–2 ml cryotubes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Management and Accreditation
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements about the IDA's quality management system and any certifications relevant to accession, control, preservation, storage and supply of biological material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some IDAs or consortia declare quality certifications (e.g., BCCMTM Quality Management System certified to ISO 9001 for accession, control, preservation, storage and supply of biological material and related information in the frame of public/patent deposits). Such certifications indicate procedural/quality standards followed by the collection.
